absent: Audit queue insertion, dequeue, retry timing, hold release and delivery thread scheduling.
Audit context creation, record formatting, filter rules and netlink message protocol.
Perf event lifecycle, privilege checks, counting, sampling and ring buffer mechanics beyond ABI layouts.
Panic tunables, notifier callbacks, crash kernel handover, reboot modes and console replay details.

findings.text: Symbol classification uses value zero for unknown, one for packet filter programs and two for out of line code such as replaced instructions and trampolines, with an additional non ABI ceiling. Unregistration is indicated by bit zero. Packet filter life cycle uses zero for unknown, one for load and two for unload, plus a non ABI ceiling.

Sampling limits are 127 frames per stack and 8 contexts per stack. Context markers are unsigned encodings of negative offsets for hypervisor 32, kernel 128, user 512, deferred user 640, guest 2048, guest kernel 2176, guest user 2560, with ceiling 4095.

Auxiliary record status uses bit value 1 for truncation to fit, value 2 for overwrite mode snapshot, value 4 for gaps, value 8 for sample collision, and high byte mask 0xff00 for monitoring unit specific format type.

Trace format selection uses zero for default compatible mode and 0x0100 for raw source format. Event file creation flags use bit 0 to avoid group membership, bit 1 to designate output redirection, bit 2 to interpret identifier as cgroup in per CPU mode, and bit 3 for close on exec behavior.

Memory access source is a 64 bit value overlaid with named bit fields. In one ordering the fields from low to high are operation 5 bits, level 14, snoop 5, lock 2, translation buffer 7, level number 4, remote 1, extended snoop 2, blocked 3, hops 3, region 5 and reserved 13. A second ordering reverses the sequence for opposite endianness while keeping identical widths and meanings.
Operation subfield encodings are 1 for unavailable, 2 for load, 4 for store, 8 for prefetch and 16 for instruction execution, positioned at shift zero.

Hierarchy level encodings use 1 for unavailable, 2 for hit, 4 for miss, then distinct powers of two through first level cache, fill buffer, second and third level caches, local memory, two remote memory distances, two remote cache distances, input output and uncached, placed at shift 5. Remote indicator is 1 at shift 37. Level number encodings run 1 through 15 for first through fourth caches, miss handling buffer, memory side cache, level zero, uncached, coherent interconnect, input output, any cache, fill buffer, RAM, persistent memory and unavailable, placed at shift 33.
Snoop encodings are 1 for unavailable, 2 for none, 4 for hit, 8 for miss and 16 for hit modified, at shift 19. Extended snoop uses 1 for forward and 2 for peer transfer, at shift 38.
Lock transaction encodings are 1 for unavailable and 2 for locked, at shift 24.
Translation buffer encodings are 1 for unavailable, 2 for hit, 4 for miss, 8 for first level, 16 for second level, 32 for hardware walker and 64 for operating system fault handler, at shift 26.
Blocking reason encodings are 1 for unavailable, 2 for data not forwarded and 4 for address conflict, at shift 40.
Hop distance encodings are 1 for remote core same node, 2 for remote node same socket, 3 for remote socket same board and 4 for remote board, at shift 43.

Region encodings range from zero for invalid through reserved, local shared and non shared caches, other agent input output, shared and non shared caches, memory mapped input output, and eight numbered memory regions 8 through 15, at shift 46. A helper combines a field value with its shift by left shifting the selected constant.

Branch record holds source and destination addresses as two 64 bit quantities plus packed status with single bits for mispredicted and predicted outcomes and transactional state and abort, then 16 bits cycle count, 4 bits type, 2 bits speculation, 4 bits additional type, 3 bits privilege and 31 bits reserved.
Branch entry extra information width allows at most 33 bits.
Sample weight is a 64 bit value overlaid with three pieces sized 32, 16 and 16 bits whose order swaps with endianness, preserving the same partition.
Audit log prefixing prepends the module name followed by colon and space to supplied format text.

Audit initialization uses three states with disabled at negative one, uninitialized at zero and initialized at one, starting uninitialized. Global enable starts off and a sticky ever enabled flag records whether enabling ever occurred.
Default policy starts off. Failure handling starts in message mode. Network namespace identifier and rate limit start zeroed and are configured later.
Subject and object security context tracking each use a count plus a fixed capacity array of security module identifiers sized by maximum module count, both counts starting at zero.
Per network namespace audit state holds a single socket pointer.

User space audit daemon connection state bundles a process identifier reference, a numeric port identifier, a network namespace reference and a deferred reclamation head. The active connection is held in a globally shared pointer reclaimed after a grace period, with a dedicated spin lock serializing updates.
Pending audit backlog allows 64 entries by default. Blocking wait duration defaults to sixty seconds expressed in clock ticks, held in a tunable with a compile time constant for the default.
Signal origin tracking starts with invalid user, negative one process identifier and empty mandatory access control attributes.
Lost record accounting and observed backlog wait time use atomic counters starting at zero.
Inode watch lookup uses a fixed bucket hash table of list heads. Formatted buffer allocation uses a dedicated slab cache pointer initialized elsewhere.
Audit delivery uses three separate queued message lists for ready, retry and held traffic, plus a dedicated kernel thread pointer for the delivery daemon.

Feature negotiation state carries version, mask, feature bits and lock word, initialized to current version with all mask bits set and features and lock cleared. Two login identifier behavior names are published for user space query.
Control path serialization uses a structure containing a mutex plus an owner pointer. A single global instance records the current holder while the mutex is held.
Single audit formatted message buffer size is one thousand twenty four bytes.

Working buffer bundles a socket buffer for formatting, a list of completed socket buffers ready to send, an optional owning context, a timestamp stamp and allocation flags. Reply descriptor bundles a destination port identifier, a network namespace reference and a socket buffer.

A predicate reports whether a given task belongs to the registered audit daemon by comparing thread group identity under grace period protection, returning true on match and false otherwise including when no daemon is registered.
Control lock acquisition takes the global mutex and records the caller as owner, while release clears the owner before unlocking. Ownership test compares the caller against the recorded owner.
A helper returns the numeric process identifier of the registered daemon in the caller namespace, or zero when no daemon or identifier is present, using grace period protection for the lookup.
Security module registration appends an identifier once to subject and object lists according to supplied selection bits, skipping duplicates already present.
Per namespace socket lookup returns null for null namespace, otherwise the stored socket for that namespace.
Failure reaction has three modes with silent ignoring the message, message mode emitting a rate limited error, and halt mode stopping the system with the supplied message.
Variadic fatal error entry accepts a format plus arguments and forwards to the argument list handler, never returning to the caller in practice.

Fatal handling moves through arbitration to a single winner, local shutdown of interrupts and preemption, announcement and diagnostics, debugger and crash capture hooks around subscriber notification and log preservation, then either timed reboot or indefinite safe loop with periodic liveness touches.

Fatal path never returns, stops or parks other processors, makes consoles verbose, may reboot after a configurable delay and otherwise spins forever with output suppressed at the end. Concurrent callers on other processors park themselves.

Debugger panic hook does nothing unless input output module is registered and automatic reboot is disabled. Otherwise it quiets lock diagnostics, flushes pending console output, optionally announces the message and enters the debugger.
Daemon connection readers use grace period protection without blocking. Writers serialize with a dedicated spin lock and defer reclamation until readers drain.
Module list registration appends to fixed capacity arrays with duplicate avoidance but no visible capacity guard in the fragment, so callers and surrounding configuration must prevent overrun.
Audit failure handling in halt mode stops the whole system. Message mode depends on rate limiting to avoid log flooding.
